Introduction
The KPZ universality is concerned with, among others, one-dimensional interacting particle systems, 1+1

dimensional random ﬁelds, where x represents the one-dimensional spatial position and t the time.

Abstract
One-dimensional interacting particle systems, 1+1 random growth models, and two-dimensional di-
rected polymers deﬁne 2d height ﬁelds. The KPZ universality conjecture posits that an appropriately
scaled height function converges to a model-independent universal random ﬁeld for a large class of mod-
els. We survey limit theorems for a few models and discuss changes that arise in diﬀerent domains. In

blocks.title: TASEP, corner growth model, and exponential DLPP
blocks.content:
TASEP, corner growth model, and exponential DLPP
This section discusses one of the most well-studied examples of one-dimensional interacting particle systems,
1+1 random growth, and two-dimensional directed polymers.
2.1
TASEP
The totally asymmetric simple exclusion process (TASEP), introduced by Spitzer [82] in 1970, is a continuous-
time Markov process on Z. At any given time, each integer site of Z is occupied by at most one particle.
A particle moves to the adjacent site to its right after a random waiting time, but only if it is empty. The

blocks.title: Hydrodynamic limit and KPZ limit
blocks.content:
The hydrodynamic limit of TASEP is about $\mathbf{h}(x,t)$ when $x$ and $t$ are proportional. For the step initial condition, $\mathbf{h}(x,0)=|x|$, Rost [@Rost81] showed in 1981 that $$\frac{\mathbf{h}(xT, tT)}{T}  \to \bar{\mathbf{h}}(x,t)$$ almost surely as $T\to \infty$, where $\bar{\mathbf{h}}(x,t) = \frac{t^2+x^2}{2t}$ for $|x|\le t$ and $\bar{\mathbf{h}}(x,t) = |x|$ for $|x|\ge t$. See Figure [1](#fig:hbar){reference-type="ref" reference="fig:hbar"} for the graph. The hydrodynamic limit $\bar{\mathbf{h}}$ is deterministic, and it solves Burger's equation [@Liggett85; @Liggett99].

Comments on universality
KPZ limit theorems are proved for many isolated examples of integrable models. In this ﬁnal section, we
discuss a few instances that universality is proved.

blocks.title: Interacting particle systems
blocks.content: The particles in the TASEP move only one site to the right. Consider a more general finite-range exclusion process in which a particle at site $0$ can potentially move to site $v$ at rate $p(v)$. Assume that $\{v: p(v)>0\}$ is a finite set generating $\mathbb{Z}$ additively, and $\sum_v v p(v)\neq 0$. In a recent paper [@Quastel-Sakar20], Quastel and Sakar proved a KPZ limit theorem for finite-range exclusion processes started from a certain class of initial conditions.
